question: Databricks Software Engineer New Grad, virtual onsite coding round (one of four parts: algorithm, cross-functional, system design and this one). The task was to **design a class and implement it together with the interviewer**: given a **class skeleton with empty methods**, choose the data structures and implement the logic with clean, extensible code. The candidate advised knowing your language's classes, objects and **method chaining** (`obj.foo().bar()`) well, and said the questions resemble Amazon's OOD/LLD style. Specifics were not shared because of an NDA.
lookingFor: Translating vague method signatures into the right data structures.
Clean class design: encapsulation, small methods, clear invariants.
Collaboration: clarifying, thinking aloud and handling follow-up changes.
followUps: How would you make your class thread-safe?
What if a new requirement changes the most frequent operation?
Mutable versus immutable chaining: what are the trade-offs?
How would you test this class?
